name: Kpatawee Falls
subtitle: Kpatawee Falls is a waterfall on a branch of the St.

facts.label: Ramsar listing
facts.value: Kpatawee Wetlands: Ramsar site no. 1629, 835 ha, designated 24 August 2006, Bong

facts.label: River
facts.value: The waterfall is on a branch of the St. John River, one of Liberia's six major rivers

facts.label: Wildlife
facts.value: Endangered Three-cusped Pangolin and Water Chevrotain occur at the site

facts.label: Local use
facts.value: Villagers use the area for picnics and meetings, palm wine, hunting, fishing, basket making and bathing

facts.label: Rice project
facts.value: Liberia and China ran a rice project inside the site to discourage shifting cultivation

facts.label: Pressure
facts.value: A potential hydropower scheme is listed as a threat; the site was not officially recognised as a tourist attraction (as of 2006)

facts.label: 2024 closure
facts.value: Police ordered the temporary closure of the falls in Suakoko after residents protested the operator Jalk Enterprise

facts.label: Dispute
facts.value: Residents accused the operator of bad labour practice and encroaching on their farmland

facts.label: Operator land
facts.value: The MoU allows Jalk Enterprise to operate on ten acres within the range and surroundings

parts.text: Kpatawee Falls is a waterfall on a branch of the St. John River in Bong County, central Liberia, inside the 835-hectare Kpatawee Wetlands Ramsar site, listed in 2006. Villagers use the area for fishing, farming and gatherings. In 2024 a dispute between residents and the site operator led police to close it temporarily.
